title: Adaptive concurrency smoothing and retroactive credit rollback for contested overages
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem statement: Customers with spiky traffic see transient overage charges or hard throttles due to short-term concurrency bursts. This ticket defines a feature to smooth per-account concurrency signals over a configurable time window and apply retroactive billing credits when a legitimate spike was transient or caused by routing/bug issues. Goal: reduce noisy invoices and support graceful rate-limit rollback when disputes are raised.
background: Current behavior enforces instantaneous per-caller concurrency limits and emits overage line items immediately. Support and Finance report an increase in billing disputes for short spikes under 2 minutes. Operations has built ad-hoc credits in the past, but we lack a deterministic automated reconciliation for short-lived bursts and contested invoices.
requirements: R1: Introduce a configurable smoothing window (default 5 minutes) that calculates a decayed moving-average of concurrency for billing and soft-throttle decisions.
R2: Allow per-plan and per-tenant smoothing policies (min_window, max_window, decay_alpha) surfaced in entitlements UI and API.
R3: When an overage is detected within the smoothing window, mark the charge as 'provisional' for up to 14 days pending automated reconciliation or dispute resolution.

R4: Implement automatic retroactive credit issuance for provisional charges that fall below threshold after replaying the smoothed signal (capped to 30% of monthly invoice or $10k, whichever is lower).
R5: Provide an API endpoint for Support to trigger manual rollback and supply audit reason; such manual operations must create an immutable ledger entry and trigger invoice adjustment workflow.
R6: Ensure billing exports and invoice line-items include metadata: raw_peak, smoothed_peak, smoothing_window, provisional_flag, and reconciliation_status.
R7: Soft-fallback behavior: if smoothing calculation service is unavailable, default to prior behavior (instant enforcement) and emit a diagnostic alert.
R8: Telemetry: emit per-tenant metrics (smoothed_concurrency, raw_concurrency, provisional_overage_count) at 1m granularity for dashboarding and alerts.
R9: Security: ensure reconciliation and manual rollback APIs require enterprise RBAC scope and are logged for audit; security_review_required: true.
R10: Backfill: provide a retroactive reconciliation job to re-evaluate provisional charges for the past 14 days during initial rollout.
acceptance_criteria: AC1: For a synthetic tenant with a 30-second spike to 10x normal concurrency, the smoothing window reduces billed peak such that provisional overage is created instead of a final invoice line item.
AC2: Admin API can list provisional charges and issue an automated credit that appears on the next invoice within 24 hours.
AC3: Rate-limiting behavior respects smoothing for soft-throttles (adds latency rather than immediate 429) when 'soft_limit' policy is enabled for the plan.
AC4: When smoothing service is taken offline (simulated), billing falls back to prior instantaneous model and an alert (SEV-LOW) is generated.
AC5: At least 95% of provisional charges processed by the reconciliation job are resolved (credited or promoted to final) within 14 days in canary tenant runs.
AC6: Audit logs show identity, timestamp, reason, and pre/post amounts for any manual rollback operation.
AC7: Billing export CSV includes required metadata fields and matches amounts shown in the console and billing API.
AC8: Performance: smoothing calculation adds less than 5% CPU overhead to the aggregation service and adds under 50ms p95 latency to per-request billing tag propagation.
AC9: Finance and Support validate sample invoices produced during end-to-end test campaign and sign off on adjustments (email confirmation recorded in comments).
scope: Implement smoothing calculation service, reconciliation job, billing export changes, UI for provisional charge inspection, and RBAC-protected manual rollback API. Canary rollout for 5% tenants followed by ramp.
out_of_scope: Modifying long-term pricing tiers, implementing new pricing SKUs, or changing plan entitlements logic beyond exposing smoothing policy knobs.
tradeoffs: Smoothing reduces noisy overages but may delay detection of genuine sustained overusage. Capping retroactive credits reduces financial risk but could frustrate large customers — need Finance buy-in on caps. Adding smoothing increases system complexity and operational overhead (debugging and replay).
rollout_plan: Step 1 (Canary): Deploy smoothing read-only signals + provisional flag generation for 5% of tenants; do not alter final invoice amounts. Duration: 2 weeks.
Step 2 (Metrics validation): Run reconciliation job in dry-run mode; compare credits computed vs. historical ad-hoc credits. Stakeholder review with Finance & Support.
Step 3 (Join): Enable provisional billing (creates provisional line items) for 10% tenants; enable manual rollback APIs for Support with RBAC.
Step 4 (Full): After acceptance, enable automatic reconciliation and credit issuance for all non-enterprise tenants; enterprise tenants default to manual review unless opted in.
Step 5: Post-rollout 30-day review to measure disputes, credit volumes, and customer satisfaction.
Rollback plan: If reconciliation job causes >1% net revenue variance for high-value tenants, automatically pause auto-credit issuance and revert to provisional-only mode.
metrics_and_alerts: M1: provisional_overage_rate (by plan) — alert if >5% of active tenants in a plan have provisional charges in a 24h window.
M2: auto_credit_volume (dollars/day) — alert Finance if daily auto-credit > configured cap for the tenant cohort.
M3: smoothing_service_error_rate — alert SEV-1 if >0.5% errors for more than 10 minutes.
M4: reconciliation_job_latency and success_rate — alert on retries >3 per job run.
M5: customer_support_dispute_backlog — track tickets referencing provisional charges.
implementation_notes: - Use existing aggregation pipeline in ENG-billing to compute per-tenant per-minute raw_concurrency and extend with exponential decay window to produce smoothed_concurrency.
- Add provisional_charge flag to billing ledger schema; ledger change requires migration with backfill job.
- Reconciliation job should be idempotent and windowed; store reconciliation_run_id in ledger entries.
- UI: Console team to add a provisional charges tab with filters and CSV export; include direct link to manual rollback action (RBAC restricted).
- Ensure privacy: do not surface customer PII in exported CSVs beyond tenant id and billing contact email hashed when necessary.
- Coordinate with Finance for GL mapping and invoice presentation text for credits.
- Security review required for manual rollback API; include hardened auth checks and audit hooks.
test_plan: TP1: Unit tests for smoothing calculation with multiple window sizes and decay alphas.
TP2: Integration test that simulates traffic spikes and verifies provisional vs final invoice behavior.
TP3: End-to-end test with canary tenant verifying backfill reconciliation produces expected credits and ledger writes.
TP4: Security test to ensure manual rollback requires RBAC scope and is logged.
TP5: Load test to confirm <5% CPU overhead and <50ms p95 added latency to tag propagation.
TP6: QA sign-off checklist with Support & Finance validating sample invoices and exports.
